decisions.reason: The necessary cross-Requirement effect is already fully represented by the candidate's message-154 MODIFY requiring E and L to follow the Hero V's entire architectural vocabulary as members of the same proprietary alphabet.
The source's second-V clarification is already fully represented by the candidate's message-154 MODIFY covering its slight elevation and restrained, non-competing echo role.
The source broadens the Hero V's governing vocabulary for other letters but does not change the existing requirement that the É accent literally duplicate the Hero V terminal geometry.
The source does not alter the second V's existing geometric derivation or right-arm character; its separate height and hierarchy clarification is already owned by REQ_SECOND_V_HEIGHT_HIERARCHY.
The source leaves the established shared peak horizon between the Hero V and É accent unchanged.
Requiring all letters to share the Hero V's proprietary architectural vocabulary does not change the existing kerning or spacing goals.
The source concerns letterform architecture and hierarchy, not the deferred champagne material treatment or its application constraints.
The source clarifies the Hero V's design-language role but does not add or remove a locked asset or change the existing revision-preservation policy.
The architectural-vocabulary clarification does not change the selected all-caps case treatment.

The client's request for an explanation of how principles are converted into letterforms is specific to the current mismatch and does not change the standing per-round rationale format or required content.
The source decision has no effect on accepted preview-image formats or delivery accessibility.
